threads.body: The override property key is currently `otel.javaagent.enable`, which is easy to confuse with the existing `otel.javaagent.enabled` config (used elsewhere) and doesn’t match the PR description. If the intent is to let users override the JDK-tool auto-disable with the standard `otel.javaagent.enabled=true`, the current implementation won’t work. Consider reading `otel.javaagent.enabled` *only when explicitly set* (non-null) to preserve the default behavior of skipping JDK tools unless the user opts in.

The stderr message says to use `otel.javaagent.enable=true`, but the agent already exposes `otel.javaagent.enabled` elsewhere. Aligning the user-facing message with the actual supported property reduces misconfiguration risk (and matches the PR description).

`isJdkToolMainClass` is only used within this package (the initializer itself and its test). Making it `public` unnecessarily expands the API surface of the bootstrap package; package-private visibility is sufficient here.
Grammar: "list of values have been" should be "list of values has been".

The inline comment refers to `otel.javaagent.enable=true`, but elsewhere the agent uses `otel.javaagent.enabled`. Keeping the comment consistent with the supported override property reduces confusion for future maintainers.

[General] These prefixes do not establish that the JVM was started by a `${JAVA_HOME}/bin` tool: `sun.java.command` contains the application's entry point for ordinary `java`/`java -jar` launches too. For example, a GlassFish entry point such as `com.sun.enterprise.glassfish.bootstrap.ASMain`, an application under `sun.*`/`jdk.*`, or a relative executable JAR named `com.sun.example.jar` will be classified as a JDK tool and the agent will return early, dropping all instrumentation by default. Please match the known tool entry points (including module/main-class pairs) rather than package or module prefixes.

replies.body:
For glassfish, the JMX metrics integration test should run and validate this hypothesis, if those fail then it means the agent wrongly self-disabled and we need to implement a work-around.

Maintaining an exhaustive list of all binaries for all JDK versions seems quite tedious from maintenance perspective, but maybe we have no choice here.
wondering if enough to just cover a few specific common things? (e.g. jstack and friends)

Have you considered that perhaps this is more a documentation issue. If people didn't use `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` they wouldn't run into this. Imo it is better to not use `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` if other options are available.

> For glassfish, the JMX metrics integration test should run and validate this hypothesis,

Funnily as far as I recall `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` is not suitable for glasfish because on windows the server startup hangs when `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` is used, on linux it will probably also hang if the agent debug flag is used. This happens because glassfish startup runs an external command, I believe it was to detect the jvm version, if that command produces a lot of output the process can hang because the output is consumed only after the process has completed.

I think `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` has fairly heavy usage via the OpenTelemetry Operator:

https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/blob/543148991f8feb169f47bbb0e37e85fbd7cb02f5/internal/instrumentation/javaagent.go#L15-L16

Glassfish/Payara does requires a specific handling, I've added this in dc88988.

I agree on the documentation side, we should probably mention that `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` or any other equivalent should be used with a limited scope and only if no other application-server or application equivalent is available.

The problem with that is that it often requires to document every application server specific way to configure, for example with Tomcat the `CATALINA_OPTS` should be the preferred option, otherwise with `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` the CLI command to start/stop the server is also instrumented.

Also, when a user mistakenly trigger this kind of issue, and even if it's properly documented and we redirect users to documentation, we can't expect all users to be aware of this when doing their setup. In case there is a dev/ops split and the person asking for it to be setup and the one doing the setup are distinct, it will be a source of silent issues and frustration.

In addition, there might be some setups where there is no alternative, for example when we can't modify a vendor-provided startup script (or they just want to do it). I think we can assume this is rare but it definitely exists.

This is why I think in a case where we know it will create issues we should err on the side of safety by default and avoid those issues.

The [injector project](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-injector) goal is to have things work nicely in the default deployment (instrument everything), it would probably be helpful for that project if these Java tools were automatically not instrumented

The initial issue reported by copilot has been fixed as invoking `java -jar app.jar` is now always excluded, same for glassfish exception, so I'll resolve this conversation.

From the following comments we can assume that usages of `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` is quite widely used, so can't just document to avoid using it:
- https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/19203#discussion_r3597279097
- https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/19203#discussion_r3581332193

We can however follow-up with documentation improvements if needed to avoid having to rely on this PR feature.

[General] Follow-up to the env var fallback above — the message should mention the env var as well, otherwise a user who only has env-var-based config is told to do something that doesn't apply to them.

```suggestion
      System.err.println(
          "JDK tool detected, agent will not be started. To override this behavior, set"
              + " otel.javaagent.enabled=true as an agent argument or system property, or"
              + " OTEL_JAVAAGENT_ENABLED=true as an environment variable");
```

[General] Should this be limited to `fromPremain`?

`JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` / `_JAVA_OPTIONS` only affect JVM launch, so the accidental-instrumentation scenario this guards against can only happen through `premain`. A dynamic attach (`agentmain`) is always a deliberate action against a chosen pid, so self-disabling there just makes attach fail in a surprising way.

`fromPremain` is already a parameter of this method, so it's a one-word change:

```suggestion
    if (fromPremain && skipJdkTool) {
```

Note this also keeps the two paths independent: if `premain` skipped, `agentClassLoader` is still `null`, so a later attach will re-enter `initialize` and start normally.

replies.body: Yes, you are right, this check is only relevant when using `-javaagent`, thus we can leave runtime attach as-is as it's use is intentional by choosing the PID.

[General] Blanket `com.sun.`/`sun.`/`jdk.` prefixes also match real non-JDK entry points, and every hit means the agent silently self-disables. GlassFish already needed one exception, and it isn't the only one: Open Message Queue (the JMS broker shipped with GlassFish/Payara, started by `imqbrokerd`) launches [`com.sun.messaging.jmq.jmsserver.Broker`](https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/openmq/blob/master/mq/main/mq-broker/mqbroker-core/src/main/java/com/sun/messaging/jmq/jmsserver/Broker.java), and its admin CLI is `com.sun.messaging.jmq.admin.apps.broker.BrokerCmd`. That's a long-running server losing all telemetry by default, with one stderr line as the only clue.

The module branch above is fine because `java.*`/`jdk.*` module names are the JDK's own reserved namespace, but the `com.sun.*`/`sun.*`/`jdk.*` *package* namespaces are not. And this branch is only reachable for pre-JPMS tools anyway — the JDK 9+ launchers pass `-m <module>/<class>`, which is exactly what the JDK 11+ and JDK 25+ entries in the test data show. So the set of class names it has to cover is closed and small; matching it directly keeps every existing true-case passing and makes the glassfish exception unnecessary:

```suggestion
    return first.startsWith("com.sun.tools.")
        || first.startsWith("com.sun.corba.se.")
        || first.startsWith("com.sun.javafx.tools.")
        || first.startsWith("com.sun.java.util.jar.pack.")
        || first.startsWith("sun.applet.")
        || first.startsWith("sun.jvm.hotspot.")
        || first.startsWith("sun.rmi.")
        || first.startsWith("sun.security.tools.")
        || first.startsWith("sun.tools.")
        || first.startsWith("jdk.jfr.internal.tool.")
        || first.startsWith("jdk.nashorn.tools.");
```

threads.body: `sun.java.command` includes the tool's full argument list, so printing `command` can expose credentials passed to tools such as `keytool` (`-storepass`/`-keypass`) in stderr and collected logs. Keep this diagnostic generic rather than echoing the command line.

replies.body: fixed by only logging command when agent debug is enabled, which avoids potential sensitive arguments exposure by default.

threads.body: [General] `System.getProperty("sun.java.command")` can return `null` (the repository already treats this property as unavailable on some systems), so this dereference makes agent initialization fail with a `NullPointerException` instead of bypassing detection as the method contract states. Handle `null` before calling `isEmpty()`.
